key_insight: Compact multimodal language models can answer structured pulmonary embolism questions better when they combine CTPA with EHR context, especially for risk assessment tasks.
clinical_relevance: This work suggests a practical path toward faster PE triage and early risk detection by using small, efficient models that integrate imaging and longitudinal patient data.
method: Built INSPECT-based benchmark with 23,248 CTPA studies from 19,402 patients
Framed 8 PE diagnostic and prognostic tasks as structured clinical question answering
Compared efficient MLLMs across CTPA-only, EHR-only, and CTPA+EHR settings with zero-shot and few-shot prompting
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that Gemma4 E4B and Gemma4 E2B performed best with EHR available, especially in the combined CTPA+EHR setting, and that diagnosis tasks outperformed prognostic tasks.
watch_item: Performance is still lower for prognostic tasks such as readmission prediction, so real-world use would need careful validation before clinical deployment.
paper_title: Efficient Multimodal Clinical Question Answering for Pulmonary Embolism Risk Assessment
